 6 weather alerts in effect Flooding, thunderstorms and travel delays: What Phoenix can expect Wednesday 
 Storm system to impact parts of Arizona into Thursday 
 Arizona faces a stormy stretch Wednesday and Thursday, with flash flooding and microbursts posing the biggest threats across the Valley. By Royal Norman Published : Oct. 20, 2026 at 6:15 AM MST | Updated : 8 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google PHOENIX (AZFamily) — A flood watch has been issued for much of Arizona, including metro Phoenix, from Wednesday morning until Thursday afternoon. Flash flooding will be likely in many locations.
 There is a lot of chatter about tornado chances in Arizona Wednesday. While a small, “spinup” tornado cannot be ruled out (but that grabs the headline), we are more concerned about flash flooding and the potential for microbursts.
 It was a similar setup last October that resulted in the huge microburst in Tempe. 
 First Alert Weather Days issued for Wednesday and Thursday continue with showers and thunderstorms. The rain could impact two days’ worth of drive times and result in up to one inch of rain around town. Most areas will get less than that.
 The mountains in the northern and eastern portions of the Valley could see more rain than that.
 The storms will be the result of a Pacific low-pressure system that’s going to essentially cut off and spend some time off the coast of California, pulling moisture into Arizona. The low will also destabilize the atmosphere, helping in the development of thunderstorms.
 Download the First Alert Weather App The latest maps from the Storm Prediction Center show most of Arizona has a chance to see thunderstorms Wednesday, but eastern Arizona has a slightly elevated chance for severe weather pegged at 15 percent.
 That area extends into the far East Valley. However, as the storm moves in, timing is certainly going to be the biggest issue.
 While high temps Tuesday in the Valley will be in the low-90s, we’re likely to see another couple of days with highs in the 70s by the end of the week.
